portInfo.description: visitkorcula.eu (EN) stresses cultural heritage, tentative UNESCO listing wording on the board site, and inter-island shipping via Jadrolinija, Krilo, TP Line, KSC and G&V Line. The Port Authority’s public pages emphasise harbour maintenance, traffic safety and concession oversight rather than a glossy cruise brochure.

climate.description: Mediterranean climate with hot, dry summers and mild winters

politics.visaRequirements: Entry and visa rules depend on nationality. Many visitors use Schengen short-stay rules, but requirements change—confirm with official government sources and your cruise line before travel.
politics.entryRequirements: Carry a valid passport (or a national ID where your cruise line and destination authorities accept it). Cruise transit formalities can differ from a normal airport entry—follow your ship’s document list.

gettingThere.fromTerminal: Korčula town harbour / ferry landing area — Korčula Old Town waterfront, 20260 Korčula
gettingThere.distanceToCity: Old town is adjacent to the harbours. Island buses/taxis exist but are not timed here. Ferry brands listed by the tourist board are for inter-island travel, not ship-to-Olympia-style excursions.
gettingThere.publicTransport: Confirm local transport options with the ship on your call date.

thingsToDo.intro: Pick one neighbourhood or excursion scale and keep time for the gangway queue on the way back.
topThings: Stone old town — board’s primary invite.
Interior wine villages — gastronomy tradition noted; operator hours gap.
thingsToDo.shortCall: Old town only. 75-minute buffer (and tender queue if applicable).
thingsToDo.standardCall: Old town + one nearby beach/village with 90-minute buffer.
thingsToDo.longerCall: Wider island loop only with 120 minutes uncommitted.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Photograph the tender number before climbing into the lanes — Korčula’s grid is dense and easy to overshoot toward the wrong quay.
